text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on July 28 in history:
1540 - King Henry VIII of England married Catherine Howard, his fifth wife.
1586 - The first potatoes arrived in England from Colombia, brought by Sir Thomas Harriot.
1588 - Many galleons were destroyed when Lord High Admiral Howard sent English fire ships to the Spanish fleet anchored off Calais to try and stope their attempted invasion.
1655 - Cyrano de Bergerac, French poet, novelist and soldier whose works combined political satire and scientific fantasy, died.
1656 - The Battle of Warsaw in the First Northern War began when Charles X of Sweden invaded Poland.
1741 - Composer Antonio Vivaldi died; best known for his concerti for violin and orchestra "The Four Seasons".

1750 - Johann Sebastian Bach, German composer and organist, died. Composer of "St Matthew Passion" and "Brandenburg Concertos", his output covered every musical genre with innovations in format, quality and technical demands.
1794 - Maximilien Robespierre was guillotined with four political allies. Known as "The Incorruptible", he played a leading role in the French Revolution and launched the "Reign of Terror".
1809 - The British under Sir Arthur Wellesley (subsequently Duke of Wellington) defeated the French under Marshal Victor at the Battle of Talavera, southwest of Madrid.
1821 - Peru declared itself independent of Spain.

1858 - The first use of fingerprints as a means of identification was made by William Herschel of the Indian Civil Service at Jungipur in India. He took the print of Rajyadhar Konai on the back of a contract.
1866 - Beatrix Potter, English author of children's books and creator of "Peter Rabbit", born.
1868 - The 14th amendment to the U.S. constitution was ratified, granting citizenship to U.S. blacks.
1901 - Rudy Vallee, U.S entertainer and film actor, born. He was one of the first to popularise the singing style known as "crooning".
1914 - Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia after the June 28 assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand at Sarajevo. This led to further declarations of war, precipitating World War One.

1922 - Jacques Piccard, French deep sea explorer, born. In January, 1960, he and U.S. Navy Lieutenant Donald Walsh set the record for the greatest ocean descent when their bathyscaphe Trieste reached a depth of 10,911 metres (35,797 feet) in the Marianas Trench, south-west of Guam in the Pacific Ocean.
1928 - Alberto Fujimori, president of Peru since 1990, born. On this day in 1990 he was sworn in as Peru's first president of Japanese origin.
1929 - Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis, widow of U.S. president John F. Kennedy and Greek shipping magnate Aristotle Onassis, born as Jacqueline Bouvier.
1934 - Marie Dressler, U.S. actress, died. She won the Oscar for Best Actress in 1931 for her performance in "Min and Bill".
1936 - Sir Garfield Sobers, West Indies cricketer and captain of West Indies test team, born in Barbados.
1938 - The 34,000-ton Cunard-White Star liner Mauretania was launched at Birkenhead, England.
1939 - William James Mayo, U.S. surgeon and co-founder of the Mayo Clinic, died.
1941 - The crisis in the Far East worsened when 30,000 Japanese troops swarmed into French Indochina.

1942 - Sir William Matthew Flinders Petrie, English archaeologist and Egyptologist, died. The author of more than 100 books, he continued excavations in Egypt and Palestine until well into his eighties.
1945 - A B-25 bomber lost in clouds and fog slammed into the side of the Empire State building, killing 14 people.
1968 - Otto Hahn, German nuclear physicist and Nobel Prize winner, died; he signed the Goettingen Declaration (1957), refusing to cooperate in possible West German construction of nuclear devices.
1973 - The United States launched Skylab 2 carrying astronauts Bean, Garriott and Lousma; they returned to earth after 59 days.

1976 - An earthquake measuring 7.9 on the Richter scale completely destroyed the city of Tangshan in China; it caused the highest quake death toll in modern times -- at least 242,000 dead and 164,000 injured.
1977 - The first oil through the TransAlaska Pipeline System reached Valdez, Alaska.
1995 - President Ernesto Samper asked the Colombian Congress to investigate whether cocaine money helped him win presidential elections in June 1994.
